title: Two sessions run in one worker pane
notes: 2026-11-09: card 7e7219dd's worktree (pane 0:3) had two Claude sessions named dashboard-terminal-4 at once: [bcbe2b] started first and busy, [af80ae] started 4 minutes later, which found the other and committed cd32e2ff before standing down. At the same time ListAgents showed other worker names freshly started and idle (dashboard-terminal-2 [c0a14a], dashboard-terminal-3 [0bbf8c]) for panes that had just been released or merged. Suspects: pane 0:3 was released after #273 merged and claimed again at once for Audit 6 (same pane number, same worker name), and the old screen session lived on in the screen host and was resumed or kept answering under the pane's name; or a restore resumed a worker whose screen-host session was still running (#226 + #235). Find which, with a test of the decision that lets a second session start for a pane, and make it impossible: one live session per pane, the old one stopped (and its scope, #255) before a new one starts. Docs: workers README, history.

comments.body: User, 2026-11-09: the machine ran out of memory and CPU just before (eight workers running tests at once, no systemd scopes installed yet). Likely path: earlyoom (tuned to kill node first) or the OOM killer took the screen host's node process or its socket, the app fell back to running the worker in-app (workers-decision-6: no host -> in the app) while the host's session lived on, giving two sessions per pane. Check that fallback: it must not start a second session while a host session for that pane may still be alive.

Evidence, 19:55: four SDK claude processes have parent pid 1 (orphaned), each in a worker worktree: 7e7219dd (16 min, 286MB), 54bfe7fe (20 min), f69bb3f4 (25 min), 4f2abb7e (69 min). Their parent (the screen host, or the app before the OOM) died and they kept running, while the panes for those cards also have sessions. Likely: the screen host was killed under memory pressure, its sessions lived on unparented, and the app started new ones. Fix both ends: the screen host's sessions die with it (or are re-adopted when a host starts again), and no second session starts for a pane whose old one may be alive.

Correction to the previous comment: parent pid 1 is not evidence of a duplicate. Pid 965649 is the live worker that just reported PR #276 (its message socket is 965649.sock), so these SDK processes are reparented live sessions (the screen host detaches them, or the host restarted). Check which of them have a second session for the same pane before concluding anything.
